shots.text: Olá! Been an interesting week.
We had a Zone Conference earlier this week, which was nice,
because I got to see all my friends that I haven't seen in a while.
Then I did a division in Capão da Canoa,
which was great, 'cause I got to see some members that I liked when I was there.
On Friday, my comp decided to start dying, so we had to go to the hospital. More of a clinic, really.
He was complaining about pain in his liver and his back, but wasn't really doing that bad during the day.
But when we got home, the pain got a lot worse,
so I had to carry him to an Uber and go to the hospital.
Once there, they gave him morphine,
and just let him sleep.
So, we'll see what happens this week.
We ended up being at the hospital for eight hours. Ten p.m. to six a.m.
And I hit the milestone of going without sleep, food, and water for twenty-four hours.
I woke up at five thirty the previous day to catch a bus, and after the hospital, slept until midday, which is when I had last eaten and drank.
Also, we were teaching a family this week, and we had asked them to read the Book of Mormon, and they hadn't yet.
So I jokingly called them vagabundos,
which I thought meant what Google Translate had told me. Which, it means bums. Which is a word I used a lot in English.
Unluckily for me, Google Translate lied to me.
In Portuguese, it is a lot stronger. And for women, it has a different connotation, one which I cannot repeat on a missionary email!
All turned out well in the end. They thought it was hilarious.
They kept calling each other vagabundos after this, and now I'm in a group chat with them titled vagabundos.
And I was spared from being beat up. In the future, I will only call people who deserve it vagabundos.
Tchau. Elder Nelson.
